root_cause: T-0702's judge (R-3, T-0702.review.md) and T-0714's architect assessment (docs/tasks/T-0714.assessment.md) both named the same unproven premise: FF-0328 (http-route-auth-coverage.sh) proves AUTHENTICATION is universal (every src/http route is withAuth-wrapped), and FF-0662 (actor-authority-deactivation-gate.sh) proves every REGISTERED authority-resolver carries the deactivated_at IS NULL predicate — but nothing proved that every data-returning route actually REACHES one of those 7 resolvers. A route can be fully withAuth-covered, tenant-scoped via resolveActorTenant (itself NOT deactivation-gated — it is on FF-0662's own ALLOWLIST as 'not authority, resolves tenant not grant'), and never call any authority-resolver at all. T-0714 found exactly this pattern live on GET /api/processes[/:id]. This task builds the missing gate.
gate_design: Per-GET-route (not per-file, unlike FF-0328) text scan: for every `.register("GET", ...)` call site in src/http/*.ts, the route's own handler BLOCK (from its .register( to the next .register( in the same file, or EOF) is checked for a reference to one of ACTIVE_MARKERS — the 7 T-0662 AUTHORITY_RESOLVERS verbatim, plus 9 derivative primitives each verified BY HAND (file:line cited in the script + ADR §2.2) to compose one of the 7 (isRecordReadable, resolveReadVisibility, resolveFieldVisibility, reportAggReadVisibility, checkReadGrant, resolveActorPrivilege, resolveRecordOp, getFileContentUrl, requirePrivilege). Per-route (not per-file) granularity was chosen specifically because a file-level check produces a live false-negative in this codebase: src/http/files.ts registers BOTH GET /api/records/:recordId/files (LIST — deliberately unauthorized, FF-NOACL/T-0521 п.1) and GET /api/files/:fileVersionId/download (authorized via resolveRecordOp) — file-level 'contains a marker somewhere' would wrongly pass LIST. A 'preamble inclusion' refinement (to catch markers referenced only inside file-local wrapper helpers like requirePrivilege()/checkAdminGrant() defined before the first .register() call) was prototyped and REJECTED: it reintroduces the same false-positive via import statements (files.ts:62 imports getFileContentUrl at module scope, which would make LIST wrongly pass again). The two live cases this limitation affects (solution-publish.ts publish-preview, notification-prefs.ts admin list) are closed by hand in ROUTE_WHITELIST §D with a citation instead — narrow-but-real over a broader-but-leaky mechanism, per the task's explicit design instruction.
whitelist_summary: ROUTE_WHITELIST has 52 entries in 5 categories, all cited in the script + ADR §4: §A pre-login (3, mirrors T-0328 register.ts), §B self-scoped (9, response keyed to the caller's own id — notifications/user-prefs/assistant-threads/list-views ownerVisibilityClause), §C vendor-signed non-actor (2, mirrors T-0328 §3.2/§3.5), §D verified-via-local-wrapper (2 live + 1 doc note — hand-verified, gate's own text-scan limitation), §E tenant-uniform config/catalog (~30 — process-defs/applications/sections/dmn-rule-tables/registry-defs/rights.ts role-catalog [mirrors the T-0328 rights.ts precedent]/spend.ts [file explicitly says 'any tenant member can view spend']/files.ts LIST [T-0521 п.1 ratified]/org.ts roster [mirrors ADR-T0658 §3.4 display-list doctrine]). §A-D verified by line-reading; §E verified by a mix of line-reading (spend.ts, files.ts, list-views.ts, rights-sod.ts) and structural pattern (definition/catalog/binding tables, not record/grant/audit) — documented as HONESTLY weaker than §A-D in the ADR; a new route is NOT auto-whitelisted by category, it must be added explicitly.

informational_vs_required: Informational. The live tree has 13 real, evidence-backed findings (see findings_not_fixed) that this task does not fix (out of scope — substrate/gate-build task per the assignment; findings become separate follow-up tasks per the task's explicit instruction not to fix them here). The gate is therefore NOT added to package.json's `fitness` npm script (a single unconditional && chain with no required/informational distinction in this repo — wiring a currently-red check into it would either need a silent `|| true` [dishonest] or would break `npm run fitness` for every future branch until someone unrelated fixes these 13 pre-existing routes, which is the exact anti-pattern the choros-fitness-mask-unmask incident (2026-07-02, FF-FL-11 hidden red behind an && chain since 06-23) already burned this codebase on once). The gate is runnable directly (`bash ci/checks/actor-active-route-coverage.sh` / `--self-test`), self-tests clean, and is documented as ready for promotion to required once the findings are triaged/closed.
live_proof: Not applicable — this is a substrate/CI-tooling task (a new static analysis script + its own self-test), not a product user-flow change. There is no UI/API behavior change to walk through live; the deliverable's correctness is demonstrated by (a) the --self-test suite (4 assertions: unmarked+non-whitelisted GET caught, marked GET passes, POST out-of-scope proven never flagged, whitelisted GET passes without a marker) and (b) the live run against the real src/http tree cross-checked by hand against ~20 individually read/verified route files (documented in the ADR), producing a result that exactly matched the hand-derived prediction before the script was even run.
friction_events: The most valuable derived ACTIVE_MARKERS (resolveActorPrivilege, resolveRecordOp, getFileContentUrl, requirePrivilege, checkAdminGrant-wraps-loadAdminContext) are NOT discoverable by grepping the 7 T-0662 resolver names alone — they only surface by reading actual route handlers end-to-end and tracing injected-dependency call chains through src/server.ts's composition-root wiring. A purely mechanical/grep-only approach to building this gate would have missed roughly half the real coverage and produced a far noisier (and less trustworthy) findings list.

A first design attempt used FILE-level marker matching (mirroring http-route-auth-coverage.sh's own FF-0328-1 style). Live-checking it against files.ts (which registers both an intentionally-unauthorized LIST route and a properly-authorized DOWNLOAD route) surfaced a concrete false-negative, forcing a redesign to per-ROUTE block granularity — documented in ADR §2.1 as a design decision with live evidence, not just a hypothetical concern.

A follow-up attempt to close the remaining per-route blind spot (file-local wrapper helpers defined before the first .register() call, e.g. requirePrivilege()) via 'include the file's preamble in the marker scan' was implemented and then live-tested against files.ts again — it reintroduced the SAME class of false positive via the file's own IMPORT statement (which textually contains getFileContentUrl for a completely different route). Reverted in favor of two hand-verified ROUTE_WHITELIST §D entries with citations, documented as a rejected alternative in ADR §3.
